name: _convert_weight_to_int4pack_for_cpu
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_convert_weight_to_int4pack_for_cpu(Tensor self, int innerKTiles) -> Tensor. The representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest defines the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation that must be supported, and its coverage must never be narrowed to this one signature. Registered ATen schema strings: aten::_convert_weight_to_int4pack_for_cpu(Tensor self, int innerKTiles) -> Tensor. Semantics: CPU-only int4 GEMM weight packing. 'self' is an int32 CPU weight matrix of shape (N, K) with N a multiple of 16 and even K; the result is a contiguous CPU uint8 tensor of shape (N, K / 2) laid out in the int4 packing layout whose block width follows the host CPU vector width (64 bytes with AVX512, 32 with AVX2). Only the low nibble of each weight element is packed. 'innerKTiles' is a required int argument with no schema default (omitting it is a rejection case); the pytest calls the operator with 0, positive, negative and int64-boundary values and compares the candidate against the native reference at each individual value, without asserting equality of results across different tile values. The operator is functional: the weight argument is never mutated. Strided or offset weight views are treated as if .contiguous() was applied first. Native validation rejects unsupported shapes (rank != 2, N not a multiple of 16, odd K), any dtype other than int32, non-int innerKTiles, and non-tensor weight arguments; those rejections remain owned by the pytest and are not expressed by this single-overload model.
